title: Go test outcomes are keyed by the IDs in each test's own name and ordered by ID
when: ReadOutcomes reads go test -json output with a subtest that carries two IDs and fails, a subtest whose name holds a slash, a subtest with an ID whose own subtest is skipped, tests with no ID, and words that look like IDs but are not, such as ST-STD-TRUST-R04. Then it reads output in which a name holds ST-FIX-INV01-T-holds or ST-FIX-SP05-Tx, a test record ID that goes on with a hyphen or a lower-case letter, in a Go test and in a Python subtest.
then: There is one outcome per ID, in ID order, with its result, its duration and the failure output as its detail. The tests with no ID and the words that are not IDs give no outcome. The run starts at the first event and finishes at the last. Each output with a malformed ID is refused, and the refusal names the word.

title: Python test outcomes are keyed by the IDs in each subtest's description
when: ReadOutcomes reads the Python runner's document with two subtests that carry IDs, not in ID order, and test methods that carry none. Then it reads documents with a result that is not passed, failed or skipped, with another format, or with no content, and go test output that is not JSON.
then: The two subtests give their outcomes in ID order, and the methods give none. Each bad document is refused.

title: The Python runner counts only a real pass as passed, and names each subtest by its description
when: The Python runner runs a suite with a passing, a failing and a skipped subtest that carry IDs, a method marked as an expected failure that fails, and a method marked as an expected failure whose subtest passes.
then: The subtests are passed, failed with the assertion as detail, and skipped with the reason, each by its description. The expected failure is skipped, not passed. The unexpected success is failed, for the method and for its subtest. Every result is passed, failed or skipped.

title: The go test -json output of two Go modules, one after the other in one file, reads as one run
when: ReadOutcomes reads one file that holds the go test -json output of two Go modules, one after the other, as the proof run writes the root module's output and then Assuring's modules': each module has a package of its own and a test of the same name, the second module has an ID of its own, and both carry one ID, which passes in the first and fails in the second. It reads the file with the root module first, and then with the second module first.
then: Both files give the same outcomes: one per ID from both modules, in ID order, and the ID that both carry is failed, with the second module's failure as its detail. The run starts at the first event of either module and finishes at the last.

title: The coverage at a commit is read from lathe check on that commit's tree alone, summed over every domain and kind, and two readings agree
when: With a git repository whose spec has three invariants of a domain and a constraint of the product, at two commits whose files differ, and a working tree that differs from both: MeasureCoverage runs the real Lathe CLI at the first commit twice, at the second commit once, at a short commit ID, and at a third commit whose spec has errors because the tests' file is gone. Then MeasureCoverage runs a stand-in Lathe that prints a reason on its standard output and another on its standard error and exits 2, and the real Lathe at a commit whose lathe.config.json says schema 2.
then: Each reading gives the counts of that commit's tree, summed over the domain and the product, and the standing of each obligation there; the working tree changes nothing. The two readings of the first commit are the same bytes. The short commit ID is refused. The commit with errors gives no measurement and a SpecError that names each error Lathe finds, never an empty coverage. Each run where Lathe exits non-zero gives a SpecError that holds what Lathe printed on both streams, its standard output cut at a limit, so the schema mismatch is named.

title: The coverage sums Lathe's counts over every domain and kind, and output whose gaps disagree with its counts is refused
when: readLatheCheck reads lathe check JSON with two domains, the product's own scope, three obligation kinds and gaps that are not shares. Then it reads output with a gap that the counts do not hold, gaps in another word, an obligation with no chain or two, a count above the total, no product, and text that is not JSON. Last, it reads the real output of Lathe 5, whose kinds carry their complexity and whose coverage scopes carry their debt.
then: The coverage is the sum of every scope and kind, and each obligation's standing follows its gaps: built only when designed. Each other output is refused, so a misread gap never counts an obligation. Lathe 5's output is read: 4 obligations, 4 designed, 2 built, 2 proved, as DS02-T01 measures the same commit.

title: The tree of a commit is written only inside its folder, and a link that leads out of it is refused
when: writeTree writes trees built with git mktree: a link to a folder outside and a folder of the same name with a file in it, a link to an absolute path, a link whose text leaves the tree, and a link that leaves the tree through another link. Then it writes a tree with a link to a file inside it.
then: Each of the first four trees is refused, and nothing is written outside the folder. The last tree is written, with its link as a link.

title: A pattern rule counts once in each domain that follows its pattern, with its standing in that domain, as Lathe counts it
when: With a git repository whose spec has two domains that follow one pattern with one rule, and a pattern rule test that proves the rule in one domain only: MeasureCoverage runs the real Lathe CLI at that commit, then at a commit that removes the pattern rule test and its test file; holdsRatchet compares the two measurements. Then readLatheCheck reads output whose scope lists a pattern rule that has no chain.
then: The first measurement agrees with Lathe's counts and holds the rule once for each domain, named with its domain: designed, built and proved in the domain with the test, designed and built in the other. At the second commit the rule falls from proved in that domain alone, and the ratchet gives one reason that names the rule with its domain. The output with no chain for the rule is refused.

title: A proof run attestation from GitHub's store verifies against the Sigstore trust root, and any altered part yields no attestation
when: VerifyAttestation fetches by the commit a real bundle from a store and checks it with SigstoreVerifier against the trust root of its day, at the change's own reference refs/pull/24/merge, with a record of commits that keeps the merge commit its signing run ran at as GitHub keeps it. Then it checks the bundle with the payload, the signature, the certificate, the inclusion proof or the log entry changed, with no log entry, against another trust root, for another commit, as no bundle and as text that is not JSON. Then a store gives a forged, the true and an empty bundle, and then the true bundle for another pull request's reference.
then: The store is asked for the commit. The true bundle gives a proof run about the commit with its 239 outcomes, change grade, signed by proof-run.yml at refs/pull/24/merge, at rekor:3614924958. Each altered bundle gives nothing at all and one refusal. With the three bundles, the true one is taken and the two others are refused. At another pull request's reference, no proof run is taken. The certificate of the true bundle names the commit its signing run ran at.

title: Of several verified proof runs the release-grade one and then the newest is taken in any order, and a store that cannot answer is an error
when: VerifyAttestation reads, through a signature check that stands for Sigstore's and a record of commits that keeps the merge commit of the commit, a store that gives two change-grade proof runs, a release-grade one and a forged one, in two orders; then only the two change-grade ones, in two orders; then a statement whose predicate is not a whole proof run; then a store that cannot answer, a record of commits that cannot answer, a store with no attestation, and a short commit ID.
then: Each order gives the release-grade proof run with its own outcome, and the forged one is refused; with no release-grade one, the newest by its log entry. The broken predicate gives no proof run. The store that cannot answer, the record of commits that cannot answer and the short commit ID give an error; the empty store gives no proof run and no refusal.

title: The code faults of a commit come from its tree and spec alone, keyed and ordered, and two readings agree
when: Commits a tree with faults of five rules to a git repository and reads its faults from git objects; changes the working tree and reads the same commit again; then commits a change that takes one of three domains from a package, renames a record's missing identifier to another missing one, and reaches the same package through another package of no domain, and reads the new commit.
then: Expects one fault per rule and key, in rule then key order; the same faults from both readings of the first commit, whatever the working tree holds; and at the second commit the same faults with the same keys, the R01, R02 and R03 faults each with another reason.

title: The SBOMs are the same bytes from the same record and name each module of it
when: With a build record with a local main module, a remote module and a replaced module: WriteSBOMs runs twice; then on a record with one module version changed, on no record, and on a record whose modules are out of order.
then: The two runs give the same SPDX, then CycloneDX bytes, each naming the executable digest and each module by its package URL, the replaced module by its replacement; the changed record gives other bytes; no record and the unordered record are refused.

title: The SBOMs name the runtime folder as the source of the runtime pin, and no source for other modules
when: With a build record whose runtime module names the runtime folder of the source revision as its source, and again with one that names the runtime folder of a STEGO checkout (checkout:registry/runtime): WriteSBOMs runs; then on a record with no module source.
then: The SPDX package of the runtime module has the comment of its own source: for the source revision, that the folder is of the source revision; for a checkout, that the folder is of the STEGO checkout that --runtime-folder named and hashes to the binary's pin; its CycloneDX component has the property stego:module:source with that source; no other package or component names a source, and a record with no module source gives no comment and no property.

title: An executable whose digest, size, build settings or modules differ from the record is refused, and each is named
when: With a build record and what was found in an executable that matches it: the check runs; then the digest, the size, two build settings and the compiled modules differ.
then: The matching executable passes. The changed one is refused, and the check names the recorded and the found digest and size, each setting that differs or is extra or missing, and the module the record does not list.

title: A source snapshot is refused on any changed, missing or added file, and each is named
when: With the files a record lists: the check runs on the same files; then on files where one changed, one lost its executable bit, one is missing and one is added.
then: The same files pass. The changed files are refused, and the check names each of the four paths with what differs, and no path that matches.
notes: The image half of ST-BLD-DS02 is ST-BLD-DS02-T03.

title: An image is refused when any digest its record names differs
when: With an image layout that matches its record: An extra file or link, changed config bytes, a missing blob, a wrong application or CA digest, a wrong diff ID, a dirty packer or a duplicate index key.
then: VerifyImage refuses each with its own reason.
notes: Not proof yet: see ST-BLD-DS02-T01.

title: The same declaration gives the same requirements bytes, whatever order the components load in
when: With the declaration and the registry of the test data set: the requirements are derived twice; then once with the registry's components loaded in the reverse order.
then: Expects the three results to be the same bytes.
notes: Run each derivation in a new process, so that a result that depends on map order is caught.

title: The requirements come from the declaration and the stated needs alone
when: With the declaration and the registry of the test data set: the requirements are derived; then again with another working folder, another host name, another clock time and other environment variables; then with a component that the registry holds and the declaration does not use, which states a need.
then: Expects each result to be the same bytes as the first, and no result to hold the need of the component that is not used.

title: An environment file is accepted only when it meets each requirement, and each unmet one is named
when: With the requirements and the environment file of the test data set: the check runs; then once for each requirement, with only that requirement's entry taken out of the environment file.
then: Expects the first run to accept the file. Expects each other run to refuse it, naming the one requirement whose entry was taken out, and no other.

title: An environment file with a value of the wrong type is refused
when: With the requirements and the environment file of the test data set: the check runs once for each of three changes: the image named by the tag latest, the egress port as the text https, and the secret orders-database as a configuration value.
then: Expects each run to refuse the file, naming the value and the type that the environment schema states for it: an image by digest, a port number, and a secret.

title: A configuration value that hides a credential or an unsafe number, and a range bound that does not parse, are refused
when: Checks one value at a time against a listed variable: a url with a user and a password, and one with a user only; a number of +Inf, -Inf, and Inf inside the range 0 to 1; a duration of -5s, with no range and with the range at most 30s; an address with a user before the host; and an integer, a duration and a number whose range text has a bound that does not parse (1 to many, at least one, at most soon, 0 to NaN). Then values of the type inside a range that parses.
then: Expects each first check to refuse the value, naming the variable and the rule (user info, not a finite number, zero or more, not an address, the range bound), with no part of the value in the message, and each last check to pass.
notes: Follow-up of the security review of PR #353: L1 (a url value holds no user info), L3 (a range bound that fails to parse was read as 0, so the range let each value pass) and I2 (a number refuses Inf, a duration refuses a negative value, an address refuses @). The registry holds a default to the same type rules (ST-SUP-INV24-T). Mutations caught (agents/followups/fu-92/mut.py, 5 of 5).

title: The fill digest is the same for the same files, in whatever order they are written
when: Write the files of untested-fill into two new folders, in opposite orders and with different modification times, and compute fill.Digest of each folder two times.
then: Expects the four digests to be equal.
notes: Digest is not written.

title: A change to any file of the fill folder or to a file name changes the fill digest
when: Compute fill.Digest of untested-fill. Then compute it again for five new copies of the folder, each with one change: one byte of policy.go; one byte of policy_test.go; a new file README.md; policy_test.go renamed to policy_check.go with the same content; and the collection in fill.yaml set to org-groups.
then: Expects each of the five digests to differ from the first digest and from each other.
notes: Digest is not written. The README case catches a digest of Go files only. The rename case catches a digest of contents only: the renamed file holds the same bytes, but its tests no longer run.

title: Recording evidence or a sign-off in the fill manifest does not change the fill digest
when: Compute fill.Digest of untested-fill. Add evidence to its fill.yaml and compute it again. Add a sign-off and compute it again. Change the evidence and the sign-off to other values and compute it again.
then: Expects the four digests to be equal.
notes: Digest is not written.

title: The contract digest changes with the slot's .proto file and with each file it imports, and with no other file of the component
when: With a copy of the built-in registry: compute the contract digest of rest-api.before_create. Change one byte of a comment in before_create.proto and compute it again. Restore that file, change one byte of a comment in stego/common/types.proto, which before_create.proto imports, and compute it again. Restore that file, change component.yaml of rest-api and before_delete.proto, and compute it again.
then: Expects the second and the third digest to differ from the first and from each other, and the fourth to be equal to the first.
notes: The types.proto case pins the decision on ST-EXT-Q04 (reading b): a digest of the slot's .proto file alone fails it.

title: The contract digest covers a file that the slot's .proto file imports only through another import
when: With a fixture component whose slot contract hook.proto imports common.proto, which imports base.proto, and a file extra.proto in the same folder that no file imports: compute the contract digest of the slot. Change one byte of a comment in base.proto and compute it again. Restore base.proto, change one byte of extra.proto and compute it again. Then compute the digest two times from copies of the folder written in opposite orders.
then: Expects the second digest to differ from the first, and the third and the two last digests to be equal to the first.
notes: The base.proto case catches a digest that follows direct imports only. The extra.proto case catches a digest of the whole folder. Resolve imports by the import paths of the registry's proto roots, as the generator does.

title: The contract digest of the fill of a command, a query or a worker changes exactly when the contract that the fill compiles against changes
when: With the inventory project of the fifth walkthrough, a manifest of each of its three fills, a fill.go of place-order that uses commands.OrderRepository, and a copy of the built-in registry as the active registry: compute the contract digest of place-order, open-orders and fulfill-orders with fill.CapabilityContractDigest twice. Then, one at a time: add a refusal to the command place-order; add a field to the message PlaceOrderRequest of proto/inventory.proto; declare the command grant-clerk with its manifest, in the same contract package; add a field to Order; add OrderLine to the entities that the worker writes; and add a comment line to components/command/component.yaml of the registry copy. Compute the digests after each change. Then, over a contract package in memory that a fill uses through PlaceOrderFill and Limit: insert a constant before Limit in its iota group, change the body of init, turn the constant group into a variable group, add //go:build linux to the file, and change the first and then the second of two var _ declarations of the file.
then: Expects the same digests for the same inputs. Expects the refusal and the proto field to change the digest of place-order only. Expects the new command to change no digest. Expects the field of Order, a shared declaration that place-order uses through OrderRepository and that the query reads, to change the digests of place-order and open-orders and not of fulfill-orders. Expects the new written entity, which no fill uses, and the comment in the component manifest to change no digest. Expects each of the six changes to the package in memory to change the digest.
notes: The contract of a command, query or worker fill is the part of the generated Go package (out/commands, out/queries, out/workers) that the fill compiles against: the declarations of its command, query or worker, the declarations that its Go files use, and the declarations that those name (orchestrator decisions of 2026-11-17 on ST-EXT-Q30). The generators write one file per package, so the boundary is drawn per declaration. Security review of PR 406, LOW-1: the build constraints, init functions and blank declarations count for each fill, a declaration counts with its keyword, and a constant of a group counts with its group; a dot import of the contract is a fill rule fault (ST-EXT-UC02-R02-T05).

title: A change to a local fill module that a signed fill reaches makes the fill stale, and a change to one that it does not reach does not
when: A project whose fill gate imports example.com/erp/workflow, which imports example.com/erp/rules/roles; go.mod replaces the two modules and a third listed module example.com/erp/other with folders of the project. The fill is tested and signed with an SSH key of the test as CurrentState gives its state. Then other/other.go changes; then MayCreate of workflow.go returns true, as in the spike; then workflow.go is put back and roles.go of rules changes. The evidence and the sign-off are written to the manifest, and the revision check of stego build (RevisionFaults) runs with the modules as signed and with the changed roles.go.
then: Expects the files of the fill digest to hold the files of the fill, module:example.com/erp/workflow/workflow.go and go.mod, and module:example.com/erp/rules/roles/roles.go, and no file of example.com/erp/other. Expects the signed fill to be qualified, to stay qualified after the change to other, and to be stale, naming the changed file of the module, after the change to workflow.go and after the change to roles.go. Expects the revision check to give no fault with the modules as signed, and one fault that names roles.go after its change.
notes: Proved by the subtest of this ID of TestLocalFillModuleDigest. spike-localfill (2026-11-27, work/agents/spike-localfill/report.md): the digest covered only the fill folder, so a change to a local fill module left a signed fill qualified. Mutations caught (fu-54): CurrentState with no fill modules (the files have no module file); RevisionFaults with no fill modules (the revision check of the fill as signed gives a stale fault); no module reached through another module (roles.go is not counted).

title: A sign-off by the listed SSH key over the current evidence digest is accepted
when: Sign the digest of the evidence of unsigned-fill with listed-ssh through ssh-keygen -Y sign, and run fill.VerifySignOff on the sign-off, the evidence and SIGNERS.
then: Expects the sign-off to be accepted.
notes: VerifySignOff is not written. Use the real ssh-keygen and gpg with the keys of ST-EXT-TD02. Sign with the SSH namespace that fill.VerifySignOff uses, so that only the key, the digest or the signature can cause a refusal in the other tests of ST-EXT-DS02.

title: A sign-off by the listed GPG key over the current evidence digest is accepted
when: Sign the digest of the evidence of unsigned-fill with listed-gpg through gpg --detach-sign --armor, and run fill.VerifySignOff on the sign-off, the evidence and SIGNERS.
then: Expects the sign-off to be accepted.
notes: VerifySignOff is not written. Use the real ssh-keygen and gpg with the keys of ST-EXT-TD02.

title: A signature by a listed key over any other digest is refused
when: With listed-ssh: sign the digest of earlier evidence of unsigned-fill, and sign the current evidence digest with one newline added after it. Run fill.VerifySignOff on each against the current evidence.
then: Expects both sign-offs to be refused, each with the reason that the signature does not cover the current evidence.
notes: VerifySignOff is not written. Use the real ssh-keygen and gpg with the keys of ST-EXT-TD02. The added newline catches a check that does not compare the exact digest.

title: A valid signature by a key that SIGNERS does not list is refused
when: Sign the current evidence digest of unsigned-fill with unlisted-ssh, and with keyring-gpg. Run fill.VerifySignOff on each.
then: Expects both sign-offs to be refused, each with the reason that SIGNERS does not list the key.
notes: VerifySignOff is not written. Use the real ssh-keygen and gpg with the keys of ST-EXT-TD02. keyring-gpg is in the test keyring, so the GPG case catches a check that trusts each key in the keyring.

title: A changed signature is refused
when: Change one character in the armored body of a valid sign-off by listed-ssh, and of a valid sign-off by listed-gpg. Run fill.VerifySignOff on each.
then: Expects both sign-offs to be refused.
notes: VerifySignOff is not written. Use the real ssh-keygen and gpg with the keys of ST-EXT-TD02.

title: A listed SSH key whose SIGNERS entry has expired is refused, as ssh-keygen refuses it
when: Write SIGNERS with listed-ssh and the option valid-before set to a date in the past. Run fill.VerifySignOff on a valid sign-off by listed-ssh over the current evidence digest.
then: Expects the sign-off to be refused.
notes: VerifySignOff is not written. Use the real ssh-keygen and gpg with the keys of ST-EXT-TD02. This catches a verification that STEGO does by itself and not through ssh-keygen -Y verify, which obeys the options of the allowed signers format.

title: A sign-off by a listed GPG key that is revoked or expired is refused, as gpgv reports it
when: Makes four GPG keys in a keyring of their own: one made with a clock of 2020 that expired a day later, one revoked with its revocation certificate after it signed, one valid, and one whose primary key only certifies, with a signing subkey that is revoked after it signed. Each signs the current evidence digest, the expired one with the clock of 2020. Writes SIGNERS with the four armored keys. Runs fill.VerifySignOff and fill.Principal on each sign-off.
then: Expects the sign-offs of the expired key, the revoked key and the revoked subkey to be refused with ErrKeyNotValid and Principal to give no identity for them, and the sign-off of the valid key to be accepted.
notes: Use the real gpg and gpgv. gpgv gives VALIDSIG and exit status 0 also with EXPKEYSIG or REVKEYSIG, so a check of VALIDSIG alone accepts both. Security review of PR #475, I1. Mutation caught (fu/standing-38): with no case for EXPKEYSIG, REVKEYSIG and EXPSIG, both sign-offs were accepted.

title: The same component content gives the same digest in any folder and file order
when: Computes the digest of one component from two copies of the registry in different folders, whose files were written in different orders and with different modification times and modes.
then: Expects the same 64-digit digest from both copies, equal to a fixed vector for a fixture component.
notes: The fixture is the small registry in internal/compiler/testdata/component-digest; its component alpha gives the fixed vector.

title: A change to another component never changes a component's digest
when: Computes the digest of component A; then one file of component B changes, a file is added under the archetypes, and the registry's own files change; then one byte of a file of component A changes.
then: Expects component A's digest to stay the same after the first three changes, and to change after the last.

title: A change of the stage or the sunset alone leaves a component's digest as it was, and a change of any other field of its file changes it
when: Computes the digest of a fixture component at stage beta with the sunset 2027-06-30; then with the stage set to alpha; then with the stage ga and no sunset; then with its stage and sunset as at first and its description changed by one word; then with its version changed.
then: Expects the second and the third digest to equal the first, and the fourth and the fifth to differ from the first and from each other.
notes: Decision on ST-SUP-Q02, reading a: the digest leaves out the stage and the sunset, so a promoted component keeps its digest when it enters at alpha. The description and version cases catch a digest that leaves out the whole component file in place of the two fields. The digest reads the raw component file, so the fixture can state a stage and a sunset before the registry loader accepts them.

title: Each component generator returns the same files for the same inputs
when: With the ten plans of each built-in archetype that ST-STD-GEN-R03-T01 makes: Compares the generator files of the plans, without main.go and go.mod.
then: Expects the same files with the same content in every plan.
notes: Not proof yet, for the same reason as ST-STD-GEN-R03-T01: 16 of the 26 components are not reached. That the generator receives only its context is shown by ST-STD-GEN-R01-T01 and ST-STD-GEN-R02-T01.

title: The assembler writes the same main.go and go.mod for the same wirings
when: With the ten plans of each built-in archetype that ST-STD-GEN-R03-T01 makes: Compares main.go and go.mod across the plans.
then: Expects the same content in every plan.
notes: One assembler serves every archetype, and the three archetypes give it wirings with routes, middleware, processes and a database.

title: The architecture model of each example service is valid and holds every part of the five aspects
when: Reads the committed architecture/architecture.json, service.yaml and .stego/state.yaml of examples/user-management and examples/user-management-rhsso.
then: Expects each model to be valid against the schema and its rules, the record to hold its hash, every component of the record, every field of every entity, one flow for each collection operation and one slot for each slot binding to be in it, and every element to name a source.
notes: The model is derived by stego apply when the examples are regenerated; this test reads the result, so a change of the derivation that drops an element fails it.

title: The same inputs always give the same architecture model
when: Derives the model 21 times from the inputs of a small service, each time with the declaration's maps and the registry parts given anew, so the maps iterate in another order.
then: Expects every model to have the same bytes, two-space indented with LF line ends and one trailing newline.
notes: Mutation caught: the fills, which come from a map, not sorted before the trust boundaries read them.

title: A model that breaks the schema or the rules between its elements is not valid, and the fault is named
when: Checks a derived model, and then seven copies: one with no layer of a component, one with the port side left, one with no phase of a slot, one with an empty aspect with no reason, one with a field the schema does not have, one with an ID that no element has, and one with a step numbered out of order.
then: Expects the derived model to be valid and each copy to be refused with a message that names the fault.
notes: Mutation caught: the check of the step order not called.
